description: 90 deduped real events from the GitHub public events API (5 pulls, deduped by id). Real distribution: 81 PushEvent, 6 CreateEvent, 3 DeleteEvent. No Issue/PR/Watch events showed up in this pull - see ecom-13-style adversarial question below for how that's used deliberately.

questions.question: List the actor login and repo name for each event.
How many events are there of each type?
Which actor has the most events, and how many?
List all Create events with their ref_type and description.
questions.notes: payload shape genuinely differs by event type (this is why root_array + variant payload matters) - CreateEvent has ref_type/master_branch/description, PushEvent doesn't have description at all, DeleteEvent doesn't have master_branch/description.

questions.question: Which repos have more than one event?
questions.notes: QuerySpec has no concept of a post-aggregation filter (SQL HAVING) - 'filters' only compiles to WHERE, which runs before GROUP BY. A correct answer needs HAVING cnt > 1. Expect the pipeline to either drop this constraint entirely (returning ALL repos) or incorrectly push it into WHERE (which would fail to compile, since a raw field can't be compared to an aggregate pre-grouping). This is a genuine QuerySpec schema gap worth adding order_by/limit's sibling: a 'having' block.

questions.question: Which organization is associated with each event, if any?
questions.notes: org is only present on 10/90 events in the sample the schema was inferred from. The other 80 rows should return NULL for org:login at query time (Snowflake variant colon-traversal on a missing key is NULL, not an error) - this tests that the compiler doesn't require every sampled path to exist on every row.

questions.question: List push events created after 2026-07-16T04:49:04Z.
questions.notes: Real pulls happened within a ~90-second window (2026-07-16T04:47:46Z to 04:49:20Z) since the public firehose moves fast - this cutoff is the real midpoint of the actual data, not an arbitrary guess.

questions.question: What branch (ref) was pushed in each push event?
List delete events and whether a branch or a tag was deleted.
List the number of comments on each issue.
targets: ADVERSARIAL: hallucination_guard - no data of this type exists at all
questions.expected_behavior: There are zero IssuesEvent/IssueCommentEvent rows in this dataset and no 'comments' field anywhere in the schema index. The pipeline should not fabricate an issues/comments path. Correct behavior: empty result, or an explicit note that no matching data/fields exist - NOT a plausible-looking query against nonexistent paths.

questions.question: How active is each repo?
questions.expected_behavior: 'Active' isn't defined. A reasonable pipeline defaults to event count per repo and says so in notes/grain_hint, rather than guessing at a more exotic interpretation (e.g. time-weighted activity, which isn't supported by anything in this QuerySpec anyway).
